user_decision: Provide a screw terminal for an external or separate signal supply and a 5V / EXT selector. User confirms their drivers can use5 V and have5 V /24 V input selection.
clarification_resolved: External driver-control supply selection is requested, in addition to3.3 V/5 V controller input compatibility.

selected_architecture.J4: Two-pole screw terminal, labelled EXT+ and GND; proposed nominal external supply5 V,12 V or24 V.
selected_architecture.supply_requirement: External terminal powers the adapter in both modes; may come from the machine's existing appropriately regulated supply or a separate PSU.
selected_architecture.S1: Non-shorting 5V / EXT selector changes driver COM+ only. It does not disconnect the logic supply or switch ground. Change only with power off.
selected_architecture.five_volt_mode: Use12 V or24 V terminal input; onboard buck supplies nominal5 V to driver COM+ through reverse-current protection.
selected_architecture.external_mode: COM+ follows the protected terminal voltage, less protection losses; for a regulated5 V terminal source use EXT.
selected_architecture.local_logic: Independent wide-input3.3 V regulator remains powered in either selector position.
selected_architecture.logic_interface: 3.3 V powered,5.5 V tolerant triple buffer accepts reviewed3.3 V or5 V controller signals; buffered60 V MOSFET sinks drive PUL-,DIR-,ENA-.
selected_architecture.host_connection: Host and adapter share ground; no external power connects to host VIO. Host VIO may serve only as a weak enable-bias reference.
selected_architecture.output_cable: Existing keyed four-wire concept retained: COM+, PUL-,DIR-,ENA-. Matching finished harness provides driver positive fanout.
selected_architecture.motor_voltage_contact: VM contact and plated hole remain omitted; no implicit use of socket motor supply.
selected_architecture.limits: 5/12/24 V are proposed nominal external-control supplies, not motor supply ratings. No48 V claim and no universal driver compatibility.
selected_architecture.backfeed_protection: 5 V selector leg requires reverse-current blocking so residual higher COM voltage cannot feed the buck. Terminal reverse-polarity/transient protection and COM discharge path require final component coordination.
